## Circular to Licensed Corporations and Associated Entities

## Business Continuity Plan in light of the Possible Outbreak of Avian Influenza and Influenza Pandemic in Hong Kong

As Hong Kong will soon move into the ordinary influenza peak season (usually from January to March and from July to August each year), all licensed corporations and associated entities are reminded to implement an effective business continuity plan ('BCP') appropriate to their scale  of  business  in  light  of  the  possible  outbreak  of  avian  flu  and  influenza  pandemic  in Hong Kong.

Information  from  the  Department  of  Health  of  the  Government  shows  that  although  the impact of ordinary influenza on healthy individuals is usually self-limiting with recovery in 2 to  7  days,  influenza  pandemic is usually associated with a greater number of cases, higher severity of illness and consequently a higher death toll. In view of the occurrence of avian flu outbreaks  in  Asia  and  Europe  recently,  influenza  pandemic  resulting  from  avian  flu  is  a potential threat that cannot be overlooked.

In  the  event  of  an  outbreak  of  avian  flu  or  influenza  pandemic,  the  business  operations  of firms may be disrupted to some extent. We issued a circular on 24 November 2003 on BCP against serious communicable diseases and another circular on 25 November 2005 on BCP reminding  licensed  corporations  and  associated  entities  to  take  reasonable  precautions  to ensure  that  their  operation  is  not  affected  by  extraordinary  events  and  minimize  potential damage to clients. A list of questions and relevant issues (which should not be taken to be exhaustive or comprehensive) were set out in these circulars which firms may usefully refer to  when  assessing  their  preparedness  for  possible  outbreak  of  avian  flu  and  influenza pandemic, such as:

- following  the Department of Health's guidance in maintaining a clean and healthy working environment;
- encouraging staff to maintain good personal hygiene;
- assigning a senior staff member to take care of the planning and implementation of the BCP;
- identifying critical systems and functions;
- establishing  an  alternative  site  office  and/or  enabling  staff  to  work  from  home (including  setting up  different critical  operational  teams  for  them  to  work  at compatible remote premises where feasible);
- back-up facilities for IT systems; and

- safeguarding  and  backing  up  vital  business  and  transaction  data,  physical  files  and tapes.

Licensed corporations and associated entities are reminded to refer to these two circulars for more details.

In  addition,  licensed  corporations  and  associated  entities  should  also  assess,  in  light  of  the possible outbreak of avian flu or influenza pandemic, whether:

- their existing BCP can handle a relatively long period of business disruption;
- they are able to appropriately close a branch office at short notice due to suspected infection by staff;
- they can maintain minimum level of services to clients with a high absentee rate; and
- they have succession plans for key staff.

Lastly,  licensed  corporations  and  associated  entities  are  also  reminded  to  refer  to  the Government  website  of  the  Centre  for  Health  Protection  (Note  1)  when  appropriate  for updated information of disease prevention and control.
